Most PC games these days (even if you buy physical media) require downloads for installation and updates, however there is a workaround.

You could take your laptop somewhere with good internet (for example your local library, starbucks or university campus), buy a bunch of games on steam and then use the backup feature to put them all on a hard drive. Then go home and use the backup to install your games to your gaming PC, saving loads of bandwidth. You will still need a working internet connection to activate most games.

Alternatively, if you can't or don't want to use the bandwidth to activate a game, you could buy games on GOG which have no DRM or you could refer to this list of DRM free games on Steam (and then backup/restore, etc.).

Beware of auto-updates, you should probably turn them off in your case. You could follow this guide to using steam with low bandwidth.
